title: Long Holds
intro: Static stretching with no kit at all, for the days you do not have a roller or do not want one.

These belong after training or on a rest day, never in the ten minutes before you play. Held long enough to matter, a stretch takes a little edge off how forcefully a muscle contracts for the next hour or so — exactly what you want tonight and exactly what you do not want before a match.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: Sharp pain, pins and needles, or anything running down a leg or an arm isn't a stretch, so stop that one.

before.label: Leave out
before.text: If a groin or a hamstring is still sore from playing, leave the hamstring and butterfly stretches out.

before.label: Swollen calf
before.text: If one calf is swollen, warm or tender and you didn't strain it playing, see a doctor the same day.

good: One leg up, hands behind the thigh, other leg flat on the floor
Soft bend in the raised knee — straighter is not better
Ankle across the opposite knee, pull the bottom thigh in
Feel it deep in the glute of the crossed leg
bad: Pulling so hard the hips lift off the floor

good: Soles together, sit tall and lean forward from the hips
Let the knees fall rather than pushing them
bad: Rounding the spine to get lower

good: Back foot up on a sofa or wall, squeeze the back glute and stand tall
Feel the front of the back hip, never the lower back
bad: Arching the lower back to get deeper

good: Back leg straight, heel down, hips forward, then repeat with the knee bent
Two different muscles, so do both
bad: Turning the back foot out to cheat the range

good: Forearm on the door frame, elbow at shoulder height, step through and turn away
Feel it across the front of the chest
bad: Letting the shoulder roll forward into it

good: From child's pose, walk both hands round to one side
Feel it down the side of the ribs and into the lat
bad: Letting the hips come off the heels

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.note: The back of the serving shoulder is the one nobody stretches — go gently.

good: Arm straight across the chest, pull it in with the other forearm
Shoulder stays down, not shrugged to the ear
bad: Pushing into a pinch at the front of the shoulder
